title: windowed-provisioning-bucket-and-tight-burst-credits
author: Hannah Patel
release_notes: Introduces windowed provisioning buckets and a ratcheting burst-credit allocator for Dedicated fleets. Adds telemetry histograms for 50/90/99 throughput percentiles and exposes new metrics for credit utilization and decay rates.
description:
Motivation: Production tenants on Dedicated often show short-lived surge patterns that cause over-provisioning when autoscalers react to instantaneous spikes. This PR adds a windowed provisioning bucket abstraction combined with a tight burst-credit allocator that enforces a slope limiter and ratcheting decay so we can: 1) honor short burst guarantees without permanently expanding dedicated pools; 2) limit oscillation when many tenants simultaneously spike; 3) surface utilization signals for post-hoc tuning.

What this changes (high-level): Implemented a windowed-provisioning layer that tracks provisioned capacity in discrete time buckets (window size configurable, default 30s) and a burst-credit manager that grants finite, ratcheting credits to tenants. Credits decay on a tunable half-life; once a tenant consumes credits above a threshold, the allocator applies a soft slope limiter to provisioning requests to avoid immediate ramp-ups. The allocator supports: hard-commit (reserved) and soft-burst (ephemeral) modes, per-tenant max-burst, and a global fleet budget that caps ephemeral bursts under contention.

Design notes: - Windowed buckets are implemented as a ring buffer per-fleet to avoid global locks; reads are O(1) and writes are amortized. - The burst-credit allocator uses an exponential-backoff ratchet so repeated bursts cost more credit over a rolling window. - Slope limiter calculates an allowed provisioning delta based on recent provision rate and a configured max_slope parameter; this prevents spikes from causing cascading evictions when capacity is tight. - Telemetry: new metrics added: fleet.windowed_provision.capacity_bucket_{index}, tenant.burst.credit_balance, tenant.burst.credit_spent, fleet.burst.global_budget_utilization, fleet.utilization.p50/p90/p99_histogram. These are exposed to Prometheus and the Console dashboards.

Compatibility and rollout: The feature is off by default; toggled by feature flag dedicated.windowed_provision=true. Default behavior preserves previous autoscaler flows when disabled. Rollout plan: 1) Canary on a small internal fleet for 48h with conservative credit caps; 2) Gradual ramp to 10% of Dedicated fleets over 2 weeks with close telemetry monitoring; 3) Auto-rollback if 5xx or latency SLO regressions exceed thresholds.

Tests and validation: - Unit tests for ring buffer behavior, ratchet math, slope limiter invariants. - Integration tests covering concurrent credit grants and a simulated multi-tenant spike to assert no more than X% of global budget is used. - Local benchmarks show median provisioning latency unchanged, p99 provisioning P95 reduced by ~12% under simulated spikes vs current baseline.

Security and perf considerations: No new external APIs. All state lives within the fleet control plane and honors existing RBAC. Memory overhead: per-tenant ring buffer kept at default 30s*2 entries, negligible at fleet scale because we only materialize for active tenants.

Commit summary: see commits field for individual entries.

Files changed (high-level): - pkg/fleet/provisioner/windowed_bucket.go (new) - pkg/fleet/provisioner/burst_credit_manager.go (new) - pkg/fleet/provisioner/slope_limiter.go (new) - pkg/fleet/telemetry/metrics.go (added metrics and Prometheus mappings) - cmd/console/dashboards/dedicated_burst.json (dashboard panels) - internal/tests/provisioner_integration_test.go (integration tests) - deployment/featureflags.yaml (feature flag default off) - docs/operations/dedicated_burst_controls.md (operator-facing runbook)

Related work: This complements ENG-1987 (queued backfill) and should reduce frequency of incident INC-2026 (brief tenant-induced warmup storms). See also PRs that added soft-reservations (references in linked Linear).

Expected impact: Lower sustained over-provisioning across fleets that experience short spiky workloads, better isolation for tenants that remain within burst budgets, and clearer telemetry to tune global budgets and slope parameters.

Risks and mitigations: Risk: overly conservative slope limiter might throttle legitimate scale-ups causing failed requests. Mitigation: feature gate + canary + observability alerts and rapid rollback path. Risk: misconfigured half-life leading to credit starvation. Mitigation: conservative defaults and operator runbook with stepwise tuning guidance.

Merge rationale: adds a production-safe, feature-flagged mechanism to reduce oscillation and improve utilization; CI green and reviewers approved.
